key_insight: Training PV forecasting models to predict multiple future time steps at once improves accuracy by capturing longer-term temporal dependencies more effectively than single-horizon prediction.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, low-overhead forecasting strategy that can improve solar grid scheduling, reduce uncertainty, and support more stable integration of PV power into the grid.
method: Combine ground-based sky images with historical PV generation data.
Train deep learning models with multi-horizon outputs instead of a single future point.
Compare multiple architectures to verify the approach is architecture-independent.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative validation across diverse deep learning architectures, showing better accuracy and robustness across the forecast horizon with negligible computational overhead.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on the quality and synchronization of sky imagery and PV history, so deployment will need careful data alignment and sensor reliability checks.
paper_title: Learning Long-Term Temporal Dependencies in Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Through Multi-Horizon Forecasting
